answer: Non-kin attestation quorums resist sybils: an identity counts only once enough established, UNRELATED peers vouch for it, and self-referential rings are discounted. A fake cluster is a closed orchard certifying only itself — pearl-strings looping inward — earning nothing, because it draws no genuine edges from outside. Honest onyx in the graph has many independent inbound vouches; a ring has only its own, so the counting rule starves it.
